stem: Which of the following best describes symptoms during the early stages of chronic kidney disease (CKD)?

options.label: A
options.text: Symptoms begin with severe pain over both kidneys
options.misconception: Kidney disease is being treated as a condition that must announce itself with pain.
options.explanation: The cited NIDDK passage emphasizes that early CKD can be clinically quiet rather than beginning with severe kidney pain.

options.label: B
options.text: Symptoms first appear as sudden loss of vision
options.misconception: An unrelated acute symptom is being substituted for the often-silent early course of CKD.
options.explanation: Sudden visual loss is not the early pattern described in the cited CKD passage; many people have no early symptoms.

options.label: C
options.text: Symptoms reliably identify disease before filtration changes
options.misconception: Symptoms are being assumed to provide an early warning before kidney dysfunction develops.
options.explanation: Early CKD may produce no symptoms, so symptoms do not reliably announce the disease before it becomes advanced.

options.label: D
options.text: Symptoms begin with persistent coughing and wheezing
options.misconception: A respiratory symptom pattern is being assigned to early kidney disease.
options.explanation: The NIDDK passage describes early CKD as commonly asymptomatic, not as a respiratory syndrome.

options.label: E
options.text: Symptoms can remain absent until the condition is advanced
options.misconception: None; the absence of symptoms is common in early CKD.
options.explanation: Many people have no symptoms during early CKD and may remain unaware of symptoms until the disease is advanced.

context: Learning objective: recognize that early chronic kidney disease can be silent. Feeling well does not establish that kidney filtration is normal; many people have no symptoms until CKD is advanced.
